what_happened: templetwo/sovereign-stack CI went red on Waves 3-5 of the project-wide audit. The Tests workflow added in Wave 3 (commit 864dae0) exposed 5 latent ruff lint errors in pre-existing code (RET504 x2 in server.py:241/266, RET505 in server.py:1717, I001+F401 in test_stage_b_integration.py). All 3 Python matrix jobs failed at the Lint step. Then after I fixed and reformatted in Wave 6 (commit 3205275), CI failed again at format-check because pyproject pinned ruff>=0.6.0 — local ran 0.14.2 but pip cache resolved an older ruff with different format-rule output.
what_learned: When bolting a stricter formatter+linter onto a pre-existing codebase via CI, the same PR must include a format-the-world commit AND pin the formatter to an exact version. Floor-pins (>=) let CI cache resolve to a different version than local, causing format-check drift even though both sides see legal output. Fix sequence: ruff check --fix --unsafe-fixes (5 -> 46 mechanical fixes), ruff format src/ tests/ (69 files), commit, push, then a follow-up commit to pin ruff==0.14.2 in pyproject so the cache key changes and CI fetches the matching version.
